items.title: Illegal electric fencing: Delhi High Court denies bail to man accused of causing 12-year-old's death
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently denied bail to a man who was arrested after the electric boundary fence installed by him on a plot of land led to the death of a 12-year old child by electrocution [Karan Singh Vs State NCT of Delhi]. In the order passed on September 14, Justice Girish Kathpalia said that the fence was electrified without obtaining a sanction from the electricity authorities. “This act was per se so imminently dangerous that the accused/applicant cannot claim lack of knowledge that it was likely to cause death of anyone coming in contact with the fence,” the Court said. Justice Girish Kathpalia As per the prosecution, the accused Karan Singh had illegally installed an electric fence carrying 220 to 225 volts on the land, without installing a regulator, insulator, circuit breaker or other safety device A trial court has already framed charges against him under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for causing culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Seeking bail in the matter, the accused said he did not have the intention to cause the child’s death. He submitted that the fence was electrified to prevent the entry of wild animals into his land from a nearby forest area. He also claimed that he did not own the land and the electricity connection was also not in his name. However, the Court noted that a satellite image of the area revealed that the electric fence was not installed between his land and the forest area, but was demarcating it from the adjacent plots. It added that police investigation revealed that local children played in the area adjacent to the land of the accused. Even a sign board warning the general public of the electrified fence was not installed, the Court observed with respect to the lack of safety measures. Further, regarding ownership of the land, the Court said that it is the accused who was cultivating and managing the land in question. Thus, the Court rejected the bail plea. Advocate Nitin Vats appeared for the accused. Additional Public Prosecutor Amit Ahlawat appeared for the State. [Read Order]

The company's longer-term vision is for every lawyer to work alongside their own team of agents. These agents would prepare the morning brief and cause list before court, keep track of matters and deadlines across a team, prioritise and draft what comes out of the day's hearings, and turn changes agreed in a meeting into a revised draft. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has upheld the eviction of a government doctor from his residence after his 82-year-old mother alleged that he and his wife were harassing her and interfering with her peaceful life [ Dr. M S Mahesh v. Deputy Commissioner ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj took note of Section 22 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. Among other provisions, this Section calls on the State to to frame an action plan for the protection of life and property of senior citizens. The High Court held that the expression "protection of life and property of senior citizens” under Section 22 is wide enough to protect a senior citizen's enjoyment of her home. The Bench added that the statutory protection extends beyond the mere payment of maintenance and can include removing any source of harassment from a senior citizen's residence where the facts justify such action. “For a senior citizen, it carries with it the right to live with dignity, and that includes the right to reside peacefully in her own home without fear, harassment or humiliation,” the Court said in its August 6 order. Justice Suraj Govindraj The Court proceeded to dismiss a petition filed by a doctor challenging orders passed by the Assistant Commissioner and Mysuru Deputy Commissioner directing his eviction from the residential premises he shared with his aged mother. The said orders was passed on a plea by the mother seeking protection under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act. The Court directed the Assistant Commissioner to implement the eviction orders within 60 days. items.title: Andhra: Bag containing gelatin sticks, detonators recovered from bus in Vijayawada
items.summary: A bag containing explosives was found on a bus at the Pandit Nehru Bus Station (PNBS) in Vijayawada in the early hours of Tuesday, September 15. The unattended luggage was noticed by a passenger, Asif Ali from Uttar Pradesh. He alerted and handed the bag over to the Krishnalanka police. Officials have recovered 46 gelatin sticks and 50 detonators from the bag. Preliminary investigation revealed that the luggage had been left on a bus that had travelled from Narasaraopet in Palnadu district, 97 kilometers away to Vijayawada. The South Zone police of the NTR district commissionerate have launched an investigation to identify and locate the person who left the explosive substance on the bus. Special teams have been formed for the purpose, while a bomb detection squad and sniffer dog were deployed as part of the search. Deputy Commissioner of Police Krishna Kanth Patil said the police were examining the incident from all possible angles and were confident of tracing the owner of the bag. The Krishnalanka police have registered a case under the Explosives Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. As part of the investigation, police are examining CCTV footage from bus stations at Narasaraopet, Guntur, Mangalagiri and other locations along the route. Further investigation is underway.

items.title: Former Andhra Pradesh Deputy CM Alla Nani dies of cardiac arrest at 56
items.summary: Former Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister and YSRCP leader Alla Kali Krishna Srinivas, popularly known as Alla Nani, died of a cardiac arrest in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, September 15. He was 56. Alla Nani, who served as Health and Medical Education Minister in the YS Jagan Mohan Reddy government, was a three-time MLA from the Eluru Assembly constituency. His mortal remains were taken to his native Eluru by road, where family members, supporters and followers paid their last respects. Alla Nani reportedly went for a morning walk and returned home before complaining of uneasiness. He was rushed to a hospital after suffering a cardiac arrest but died during treatment. His body will be cremated in Eluru on Wednesday, September 16. He is survived by his wife Alla Rekha and two sons, Alla Kalikrishna Manichandra and Alla Ashish. Born on December 30, 1969, in Eluru in the erstwhile West Godavari district, Alla Nani was the son of Alla Suryachandra Rao and Nagamani. He completed his schooling at KP High School in Eluru in 1985 and his Intermediate education at Sir CR Reddy College in 1988. He later enrolled for a BA at Andhra University but discontinued his studies. Alla Nani contested the Eluru Assembly seat on a Congress ticket in 1994 and 1999 but lost both elections. He was elected MLA for the first time in 2004, defeating TDP candidate Ambika Krishna by 33,053 votes. He retained the seat in the 2009 Assembly elections. He quit the Congress in 2012 and joined the YSR Congress Party the following year. In 2014, he became the YSRCP district president, while he also contested the Eluru Assembly seat that year and lost. Alla Nani subsequently entered the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council after being elected as an MLC under the MLA quota in 2017. He returned to the Assembly in 2019 after winning the Eluru seat on a YSRCP ticket. After the YSRCP formed the government in 2019, Alla Nani was appointed Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Health, Family Welfare and Medical Education. He held the health portfolio through the COVID-19 pandemic and continued in the post until the Cabinet was reshuffled in April 2022. Alla Nani lost the Eluru Assembly seat in the 2024 elections by more than 62,000 votes. He subsequently resigned from the YSRCP and its district president post in August 2024, saying he was leaving politics. He joined the Telugu Desam Party in February 2025. items.title: Telangana CM Revanth seeks Aga Khan Foundation’s help for Musi revival
items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Tuesday, September 15, sought the Aga Khan Foundation’s support for the state government’s plans to rejuvenate the Musi river and develop its surrounding areas. During a meeting with Prince Rahim Aga Khan V, the 50th hereditary Imam of the Shia Ismaili Muslims, in Hyderabad on September 15, CM Revanth proposed that the Foundation undertake the restoration of the old Osmania General Hospital building and City College, both located along the Musi. The government plans to shift Osmania General Hospital to a new facility at Goshamahal Stadium and preserve the existing structure as a heritage building. CM Revanth also invited Prince Rahim Aga Khan to the Invest Telangana global summit scheduled for December 7. He proposed cooperation between the Foundation and the State in education, healthcare and tourism. The Chief Minister highlighted the Aga Khan Foundation’s role in restoring heritage sites in Hyderabad, including the Legislative Council building, and recalled the association of the late Prince Karim Aga Khan IV with the city. Prince Rahim Aga Khan sought details about the proposed Bharat Future City. CM Revanth said its master plan was being prepared by Singapore-based consultants and that the project would be developed as a net-zero city with a 15,000-acre green zone. He also said several global companies, including Amazon Web Services, had begun establishing operations there. Chief Minister’s Advisor K Ramakrishna Rao also briefed the Aga Khan about agreements reached with international universities during recent visits to the UK and US, including proposed facilities by London Business School and Harvard University.

Journalists working morning shift in the Reporter TV newsroom have alleged that the police took away their phones during the search. The searches were carried out based on a court warrant, according to investigation officer Bijoy Chandran. The SIT is probing allegations of financial loss to the government in connection with the initiative to bring Messi and the Argentina national football team to Kerala. “This search is based on the inquiry into the alleged loss caused to the government in connection with the promise to bring Messi to Kerala. He alleged that those at the premises were not cooperating with the police. “They are not cooperating with us. They are not ready to accept the search notice or open the premises for us. We have also informed them that they can communicate only in our presence until the search is over,” he said. The police reached the Reporter TV office in Kalamassery in the early hours as part of the searches at five locations. The SIT was formed to examine alleged irregularities surrounding the previous government's efforts to bring the Argentina team and Messi to Kerala. Its investigation covers the financial transactions associated with the proposed event, the process through which the private sponsor was selected and allegations of financial loss to the state. The probe had also flagged an alleged tax liability of Rs 25.78 crore involving Reporter Broadcasting Company Private Limited. The financial transactions linked to the proposed event included a reported remittance of around Rs 126 crore to the Argentine Football Association (AFA).
